what_it_does: Many chips handle sensitive data — like encryption keys — and attackers can steal those secrets by measuring how much power the chip draws moment-to-moment; this is called a power side-channel attack. The problem is that current defenses either slow the chip down a lot or leave some leakage paths open. POLARIS is a framework that uses Explainable AI (XAI — a branch of machine learning that not only makes predictions but also explains which inputs drove each prediction) to find exactly which power patterns are most exploitable. It then automatically builds a training dataset without any human labeling and trains a 'masking' model that disguises those dangerous power signatures. By targeting only the most revealing patterns, POLARIS reduces leakage more efficiently than approaches that try to suppress all power variation uniformly.
